reference: Own python solution of the coupled I-135/Xe-135 equations after shutdown using the constants read out of the tool (lambda_I 2.926e-5 1/s, lambda_Xe 2.106e-5 1/s, gamma_I 0.0639, gamma_Xe 0.00237, sigma_a^Xe 2.65e-18 cm2, Sigma_f 0.0616 1/cm, nu 2.43).  Two structurally different routes: (1) the closed-form two-exponential solution with the peak located by brentq on dX/dt and the dead-time edges by brentq on |rho|-margin; (2) a direct numerical integration (scipy solve_ivp, LSODA, rtol 1e-12) with the peak located by bounded minimisation of the dense output.  The two routes agree to 1.2e-7 in peak time and 1.8e-12 in peak reactivity.
reference_citations: J.R. Lamarsh and A.J. Baratta, "Introduction to Nuclear Engineering", 3rd ed., Sec. 8.4 "Fission product poisoning" - I-135/Xe-135 balance equations, equilibrium xenon and the post-shutdown xenon peak.
J.J. Duderstadt and L.J. Hamilton, "Nuclear Reactor Analysis", Wiley (1976), Sec. 15-2 (xenon poisoning, dead time).
US DOE Fundamentals Handbook, Nuclear Physics and Reactor Theory (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Module 3 - xenon-135 peak ~10-11 h after shutdown and the xenon dead time.
tolerance: reactivities 0.5 pcm (the tool prints integer pcm); peak time 0.0064 h and dead time 0.0128 h (2 printed decimals plus the 5 s RK4 grid on which the tool locates them).

cases.note: below phi = lambda_Xe*gamma_Xe/(gamma_I*sigma_a) = 2.948e+11 n/cm2/s the post-shutdown xenon monotonically decays and there is no peak at all; the flux slider bottoms out at 1e12

classical result: at high pre-shutdown flux the xenon peak occurs ~11.3 h after shutdown.  With the half-lives this tool uses (I-135 6.580 h, Xe-135 9.142 h) the infinite-flux limit of the peak time is ln(lI/lX)/(lI-lX) = 11.140 h
